brief.meaningEn: From the earliest stage of life, often used to question whether an activity must start extremely young.
brief.meaningZh: 從出生後最早的時期開始，常用來討論某活動是否必須極早開始。
brief.grammar: From the cradle is a fixed time phrase; pair it with start, learn, be taught or a similar verb. It does not itself specify an exact age.
brief.register: Everyday parenting and education debate; a sports adviser corrects an exaggerated claim about when children must start.
brief.boundaryZh: 指極早年紀，不是精確年齡，也不能推斷開始較晚的人沒有成功機會。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不是字面上在搖籃內訓練；片語不表示家長必須安排嬰兒上課。
brief.outcomeZh: 能辨別「極早開始」與「必須極早開始」兩種不同說法。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 188, row 5; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: Elite training does not begin from the cradle.

listening.en: A parent thought violin lessons had to start from the cradle. The teacher explained that beginners in primary school can still learn well with suitable practice.
listening.zh: 一名家長以為小提琴課必須從襁褓時期開始。老師解釋，只要練習方法合適，小學生初學仍能學得好。
listening.promptZh: from the cradle 在這裏表示甚麼？

options.en: From the very beginning of life.
options.zh: 從生命最早的時期開始。

options.en: Only after primary school.
options.zh: 只在小學畢業後開始。

options.en: At one exact age set by the teacher.
options.zh: 在老師指定的某個確切年齡開始。

options.en: Only while using a physical cot.
options.zh: 只在使用真正嬰兒床時開始。

listening.explanationZh: 片語指極早年紀，不指定確切歲數。

reply.promptEn: Does every chess player need lessons as a baby? The club coach says several strong players joined in their teens and improved through regular practice.
reply.promptZh: （每位棋手都須在嬰兒時期上課嗎？學會教練說，有幾位實力很強的棋手到十多歲才加入，並靠定期練習進步。）

options.en: Starting in the teens can still allow progress.
options.zh: 十多歲開始仍可進步。

options.en: The examples challenge the idea of a required infant start.
options.zh: 這些例子質疑必須在嬰兒期開始的說法。

options.en: Chess does not have to be taught from the cradle.
options.zh: 棋藝不一定要從襁褓時期教起。

options.en: Regular practice matters in the coach’s examples.
options.zh: 教練舉的例子顯示定期練習很重要。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都根據十多歲起步仍有進步作答。

scene.promptZh: 一名游泳教練說，少年初學者也可掌握技巧。哪句符合她的意思？

options.en: Swimming need not begin from the cradle.
options.zh: 游泳不必從襁褓時期開始。

options.en: A teenager cannot learn to swim.
options.zh: 青少年不可能學游泳。

options.en: Every swimmer must start at a precise age.
options.zh: 所有泳手必須在同一確切年齡開始。

scene.explanationZh: 片語用於極早開始；少年仍可學，表示非必需。

contrast.promptZh: 哪句把 from the cradle 用得最審慎？

options.en: It names an exact age of two months.
options.zh: 它指精確的兩個月大。

options.en: It refers broadly to very early life, not a required start date.
options.zh: 它大致指生命最早期，並非規定的起步日期。

options.en: It means every later beginner will fail.
options.zh: 它表示所有較遲起步的人都會失敗。

contrast.explanationZh: 片語是寬泛時間說法，不是成敗定律。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「from the cradle 證明一定要嬰兒時上課。」哪句最準確？

options.en: From the cradle describes an extremely early start, but does not say that start is necessary.
options.zh: 從襁褓時期指極早開始，但沒有說那是必需的。

options.en: It always fixes the start at six months old.
options.zh: 它總把開始年齡定在六個月。

options.en: It rules out learning as a teenager.
options.zh: 它排除十多歲才開始學習。

dialogue.explanationZh: 極早開始與必須極早開始不同。

speaking.en: The coach said that learning to balance on a board need not begin from the cradle; older beginners can practise safely too.
speaking.zh: 教練說，學習滑板上的平衡不必從襁褓時期開始；年紀較大的初學者也可安全練習。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說出較年長初學者仍可怎樣學習。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：舞蹈學校廣告聲稱「必須兩歲前開始，否則永遠跳不好」；導師舉出一位十二歲開始、經四年練習後能完成公開演出的學生。用英文反駁必須極早開始，但不要保證人人會成功。
writing.selfCheckZh: 寫出廣告主張兩歲前必須開始、學生十二歲起步、練習四年後公開演出；勿保證人人成功。

examples.en: Dance does not have to start from the cradle: one student began at twelve and performed publicly after four years of practice, although that example does not guarantee the same result for everyone.
examples.zh: 舞蹈不必從襁褓時期開始：一名學生十二歲起步，練習四年後能公開演出；但這個例子不保證人人有相同結果。

examples.en: The advert insists on starting before age two, but training from the cradle is not the only path. A pupil who began at twelve reached a public performance after four years of practice.
examples.zh: 廣告堅稱要在兩歲前開始，但從襁褓時期訓練並非唯一途徑。一名十二歲起步的學生練習四年後已能公開演出。

takeaways.en: From the cradle means from the earliest period of life.
takeaways.zh: 從襁褓時期，指從生命最早階段開始。

takeaways.en: Starting from the cradle is not necessarily required for later learning.
takeaways.zh: 日後能否學習，不一定取決於是否從襁褓時期開始。

notes: AI-authored provisional draft; independent English, Chinese, media and QA review remain pending. Guide-written source provenance; newly written practice. No human or release approval is implied.

lessons.titleZh: 熟悉得像環境的一部分

brief.meaningEn: So long-established and familiar in a place or group that people expect it to be there.
brief.meaningZh: 在某處或群體存在已久，熟悉到大家自然預期它會在。
brief.grammar: Be part of the furniture in/at a place; subject can be a person, activity or feature. Figurative furniture does not imply inanimate status.
brief.register: Informal school and workplace talk; an alumnus explains why a decades-old school event feels inseparable from the campus.
brief.boundaryZh: 側重長久、熟悉及融入環境；不等於每個人都喜歡它，也不是單指受歡迎。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不是字面上變成桌椅，也不能因一日內常見便說是長久一部分。
brief.outcomeZh: 能以時間與群體習慣證明某事成為環境中熟悉的常態。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 189, row 5; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: Football is part of the furniture in many schools.

listening.en: For thirty years, the school bell has played the same melody at lunch. Former students recognise it at once; it has become part of the furniture on campus.
listening.zh: 三十年來，學校午飯鐘聲都播放同一段旋律。舊生一聽便認得，它已成為校園裏熟悉得像環境一部分的聲音。
listening.promptZh: part of the furniture 表示甚麼？

options.en: A familiar, long-established part of campus life.
options.zh: 校園生活中存在已久、大家熟悉的一部分。

options.en: A new feature installed this morning.
options.zh: 今早才加設的新安排。

options.en: A song played only once and forgotten.
options.zh: 只播過一次便被忘記的歌曲。

options.en: An actual chair made from a bell.
options.zh: 用鐘聲製成的真正椅子。

listening.explanationZh: 三十年不變、舊生立刻認得，支持長久熟悉。

reply.promptEn: Why do former students ask about the morning chess table? The same table has been open in the courtyard every school day for twenty-five years, and generations learned there.
reply.promptZh: （舊生為何問起早上的棋桌？同一張棋桌二十五年來每個上課天都設在庭院，幾代學生曾在那裏學棋。）

options.en: It has become a familiar school fixture.
options.zh: 它已成為熟悉的校園常態。

options.en: Generations expect to find it there.
options.zh: 幾代人都預期在那裏見到它。

options.en: The chess table is part of the furniture at the school.
options.zh: 棋桌已是學校裏熟悉得像環境一部分的存在。

options.en: Its long history explains the alumni’s interest.
options.zh: 悠久歷史解釋了舊生為何關心它。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都根據長年持續及群體熟悉作答。

scene.promptZh: 圖書館同一位義工每週講故事已有二十年，家長和舊讀者都認得她。哪句貼切？

options.en: She is part of the furniture at the library.
options.zh: 她在圖書館已熟悉得像環境的一部分。

options.en: She joined the library yesterday.
options.zh: 她昨天才加入圖書館。

options.en: She is a literal piece of library furniture.
options.zh: 她是圖書館裏真正的家具。

scene.explanationZh: 片語也可形容長年出現、人人熟悉的人。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不足以支持 part of the furniture？

options.en: A breakfast stall has served the same block for forty years.
options.zh: 早餐攤檔在同一街區經營四十年。

options.en: A new poster appears for one afternoon, then disappears.
options.zh: 新海報只貼了一個下午便拆除。

options.en: A school ritual has continued for three generations.
options.zh: 學校傳統延續了三代。

contrast.explanationZh: 短暫出現，沒有長久熟悉的基礎。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「part of the furniture 一定表示大家都喜歡那件事。」哪句較準確？

options.en: Being part of the furniture means being familiar and established; opinions can differ.
options.zh: 成為環境中熟悉的一部分，重點是存在已久；大家的喜好仍可不同。

options.en: It guarantees everyone likes it.
options.zh: 它保證人人喜歡。

options.en: It applies only to sofas.
options.zh: 它只適用於梳化。

dialogue.explanationZh: 熟悉和受歡迎不是同一判斷。

speaking.en: The old clock in the station hall is part of the furniture for regular commuters; they expect its chime every morning.
speaking.zh: 車站大堂的舊鐘對常客而言已熟悉得像環境的一部分；他們每天早上都預期聽到鐘聲。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再指出通勤者每天預期聽到甚麼。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：一個社區劇團每年在同一廣場免費演出，已連續二十八年；居民把這場演出視為夏季常態，但有人不喜歡音量。用英文說明它的地位，不要聲稱人人喜歡。
writing.selfCheckZh: 寫出每年同一廣場、二十八年、居民視為夏季常態，以及有人嫌聲量大。

examples.en: After twenty-eight years of free summer performances in the same square, the theatre group is part of the furniture in the neighbourhood, even though some residents dislike the volume.
examples.zh: 劇團在同一廣場免費夏季演出二十八年後，已成為社區熟悉的常態，雖然部分居民不喜歡音量。

examples.en: The annual free show has been held in the same square for twenty-eight years, making it part of the furniture in the neighbourhood each summer; familiarity does not mean everyone enjoys its loud sound.
examples.zh: 免費演出每年在同一廣場舉行，延續了二十八年，每逢夏季都成為社區熟悉的常態；熟悉不代表人人喜歡其響亮聲音。

takeaways.en: Part of the furniture means long-established and familiar in a place.
takeaways.zh: 熟悉得像環境的一部分，指在某處存在已久。

takeaways.en: Being part of the furniture does not guarantee universal approval.
takeaways.zh: 成為熟悉常態，不保證得到所有人喜歡。

notes: AI-authored provisional draft; independent English, Chinese, media and QA review remain pending. Guide-written source provenance; newly written practice. No human or release approval is implied.

brief.meaningEn: Erase a previous record or set of grievances and start again without treating them as ongoing obstacles.
brief.meaningZh: 把過往紀錄或恩怨一筆勾銷，重新開始。
brief.grammar: Wipe the slate clean; wiped the slate clean in the past. Slate is singular and clean completes the idiom. A new event does not automatically do this.
brief.register: Everyday relationship and institutional discussion; a committee chair distinguishes a new proposal from formally resolving old complaints.
brief.boundaryZh: 真正重新開始須處理舊紀錄或恩怨；新潮流、新名稱或換人，不會自動抹去過去。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不是擦黑板，也不代表過去發生的事被否認或後果自動消失。
brief.outcomeZh: 能判斷舊問題是否已獲處理，以及是否有理由說能重新開始。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 189, row 8; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: A new trend will not wipe the slate clean.

listening.en: A club changed its logo, but members’ unresolved complaints about fees remained. The new design did not wipe the slate clean.
listening.zh: 社團換了標誌，但會員對收費的投訴仍未處理。新設計並沒有把舊問題一筆勾銷。
listening.promptZh: did not wipe the slate clean 表示甚麼？

options.en: The change did not erase the unresolved issues.
options.zh: 改動沒有抹去未解決的問題。

options.en: All fee complaints were formally resolved.
options.zh: 所有收費投訴均正式解決。

options.en: The club bought a new noticeboard.
options.zh: 社團買了新告示板。

options.en: Members forgot the dispute at once.
options.zh: 會員立即忘記爭議。

listening.explanationZh: 標誌換了，收費投訴卻仍在。

reply.promptEn: Can the project team start fresh after last year’s dispute? The two sides have reviewed every complaint, corrected the accounts and agreed in writing to close the old case.
reply.promptZh: （去年爭議後，項目團隊能重新開始嗎？雙方已逐項檢討投訴、更正帳目，並書面同意結束舊案。）

options.en: They have dealt with the earlier dispute.
options.zh: 他們已處理先前爭議。

options.en: The written agreement supports a fresh start.
options.zh: 書面協議支持重新開始。

options.en: They have agreed to wipe the slate clean.
options.zh: 他們已同意把舊事一筆勾銷，重新開始。

options.en: The old case is closed after correction and review.
options.zh: 舊案在更正及檢討後結束。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都根據具體處理及書面結案作答。

scene.promptZh: 一間合作社只是改名，舊欠款仍未還。哪句最準確？

options.en: The name change has not wiped the slate clean.
options.zh: 改名沒有把舊帳一筆勾銷。

options.en: The debts have vanished automatically.
options.zh: 欠款已自動消失。

options.en: A fresh sign settles every old obligation.
options.zh: 新招牌便可清償所有舊責任。

scene.explanationZh: 改名不會自行解決舊欠款。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個情境最能支持 wipe the slate clean？

options.en: A manager ignores every complaint but launches a new slogan.
options.zh: 經理不理投訴，卻推出新口號。

options.en: Both parties settle outstanding claims and agree to restart without old penalties.
options.zh: 雙方處理未解決申索，同意不再以舊罰則阻礙重新開始。

options.en: A club repaints its door while leaving disputes open.
options.zh: 社團重新油門，爭議卻仍未處理。

contrast.explanationZh: 處理舊事並同意重新開始，才有真正重置。

dialogue.promptZh: 有人說：「新安排一定 wipe the slate clean。」哪句回應較準確？

options.en: We can wipe the slate clean only if we first address the outstanding issues together.
options.zh: 只有先一起處理尚未解決的問題，我們才能把舊事一筆勾銷。

options.en: Every new plan erases previous obligations.
options.zh: 任何新計劃都抹去先前責任。

options.en: The idiom requires washing a real writing slate.
options.zh: 這片語要求清洗真正的石板。

dialogue.explanationZh: 更新安排與解決舊事不是一回事。

speaking.en: After both families settled the repair bill and apologised, they chose to wipe the slate clean and plan the next event together.
speaking.zh: 兩個家庭結清維修費並道歉後，選擇把舊事一筆勾銷，一起籌辦下一次活動。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說出他們重新合作前完成哪兩件事。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：學生報紙與攝影學會曾因未署名照片爭執；編輯已補上署名、公開道歉，雙方同意把該爭議結案並共同籌辦展覽。用英文說明重新開始的依據，不要說照片從未被錯用。
writing.selfCheckZh: 寫出未署名照片的爭議、補署名、公開道歉、雙方結案並合作；不否認過去錯誤。

examples.en: After the paper added the missing photo credit and apologised publicly, both clubs agreed to wipe the slate clean over that dispute and organise an exhibition together.
examples.zh: 學生報紙補上遺漏的照片署名並公開道歉後，兩個學會同意把該爭議一筆勾銷，合辦展覽。

examples.en: The uncredited photograph caused a dispute, but the editors corrected the credit and apologised. With both groups agreeing to close the case, they could wipe the slate clean and plan a joint exhibition.
examples.zh: 未署名照片曾引起爭議，但編輯補上署名並道歉。雙方同意結案後，便可把舊事一筆勾銷，共同籌辦展覽。

takeaways.en: Wipe the slate clean means resolve or set aside past issues for a fresh start.
takeaways.zh: 一筆勾銷，指處理或放下舊事後重新開始。

takeaways.en: A new trend cannot wipe the slate clean while earlier problems remain.
takeaways.zh: 若舊問題仍在，新潮流不能自動把過去一筆勾銷。

notes: AI-authored provisional draft; independent English, Chinese, media and QA review remain pending. Guide-written source provenance; newly written practice. No human or release approval is implied.

brief.meaningEn: Draw a share of attention away from someone or something that previously had most of it.
brief.meaningZh: 從原本受矚目的對象那裏分去部分注意力或風頭。
brief.grammar: Steal some of the limelight; some limits the amount diverted. The subject is the newcomer or alternative attracting attention.
brief.register: Informal event and media commentary; a reviewer compares a new act with the familiar headline attraction.
brief.boundaryZh: 指注意力被分走一部分，不等於原本主角完全失去觀眾，也不必有惡意。
brief.misconceptionZh: 沒有真正偷竊或聚光燈；須有原本較受矚目的對象供比較。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指出誰原先佔據焦點、誰分走部分關注，以及份額而非全面取代。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 189, row 9; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: New sports may steal some of the limelight.

listening.en: The annual orchestra concert remained the festival’s main draw, but a new puppet troupe filled a smaller hall and stole some of the limelight.
listening.zh: 年度管弦樂音樂會仍是節慶的主要賣點，但新木偶劇團坐滿了較小的演出廳，分走了部分風頭。
listening.promptZh: stole some of the limelight 表示甚麼？

options.en: The troupe drew some attention from the main attraction.
options.zh: 劇團從主要節目分走部分關注。

options.en: The orchestra lost every listener.
options.zh: 管弦樂團失去所有觀眾。

options.en: Someone physically took stage lamps.
options.zh: 有人實際拿走舞台燈。

options.en: The troupe intentionally sabotaged the concert.
options.zh: 劇團蓄意破壞音樂會。

listening.explanationZh: 新劇團受注目，但音樂會仍是主要賣點。

reply.promptEn: Is the long-running science show still the fair’s headline event? Yes, but the first robotics demonstration also drew a long queue and appeared in several reviews.
reply.promptZh: （多年來的科學表演仍是博覽會主打活動嗎？是，但首次機械人示範也吸引了長龍，並見於多篇評論。）

options.en: The new demonstration attracted part of the audience’s attention.
options.zh: 新示範吸引了觀眾的部分注意。

options.en: The established show remains the headline event.
options.zh: 舊表演仍是主打活動。

options.en: The robotics demonstration stole some of the limelight.
options.zh: 機械人示範分去了部分風頭。

options.en: Both the familiar and new events received notice.
options.zh: 原有及新活動都受到關注。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都承認舊節目仍主打，新節目分得關注。

scene.promptZh: 頒獎禮仍以電影獎項為主，卻有新設短片獎廣受採訪。哪句貼切？

options.en: The short-film award stole some of the limelight.
options.zh: 短片獎分走了部分風頭。

options.en: The film awards lost all coverage.
options.zh: 電影獎項完全失去報道。

options.en: The short-film team stole a lighting fixture.
options.zh: 短片團隊偷了燈具。

scene.explanationZh: 新項目分得部分媒體關注，原主項仍在。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不符合 steal some of the limelight？

options.en: A new soloist receives press attention alongside the established star.
options.zh: 新獨奏家與知名明星同樣得到傳媒關注。

options.en: An alternative event attracts some visitors from the traditional main show.
options.zh: 另一活動從傳統主場節目吸引部分觀眾。

options.en: An unnoticed side stall gets no visitors or mentions.
options.zh: 不起眼的小攤檔無訪客，也無人提及。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「這句一定表示舊主角被完全取代。」哪句回應較準確？

options.en: To steal some of the limelight is to gain a share of attention, not necessarily replace the original draw.
options.zh: 分走部分風頭是取得部分關注，不一定取代原本主角。

options.en: It always means the original has no audience left.
options.zh: 它一定表示原本主角再無觀眾。

options.en: It requires a literal theft of lights.
options.zh: 它要求實際偷走燈光。

dialogue.explanationZh: some 限定了被分走的注意份額。

speaking.en: The veteran singer still closed the concert, but the new duet stole some of the limelight when its clip circulated widely afterward.
speaking.zh: 資深歌手仍為音樂會壓軸，但新二重唱的片段事後廣泛流傳，分走了部分風頭。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再指出誰仍壓軸，以及誰分得關注。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：地方美食節的老牌麵檔仍有最長隊伍；首次參展的豆腐攤獲三家報章報道，吸引部分訪客，但未取代麵檔。用英文描述注意力如何分配。
writing.selfCheckZh: 寫出老牌麵檔仍最受歡迎、新豆腐攤獲三家報章報道並吸引部分訪客、未全面取代。

examples.en: The old noodle stall still had the longest queue, but a first-time tofu stall stole some of the limelight after three newspapers covered it and some visitors came to try it.
examples.zh: 老牌麵檔仍有最長隊伍，但首次參展的豆腐攤獲三家報章報道，吸引部分訪客試食，分走了部分風頭。

examples.en: Three newspapers covered the new tofu stall, which stole some of the limelight from the established noodle stall. Some visitors tried it, although the noodle queue remained the longest.
examples.zh: 三家報章報道新豆腐攤，使它從老牌麵檔分走部分風頭。有訪客前來試食，但麵檔隊伍仍是最長。

takeaways.en: Steal some of the limelight means draw a share of attention from an established focus.
takeaways.zh: 分走部分風頭，指從原本焦點取得部分關注。

takeaways.en: Stealing some of the limelight does not mean the original attraction vanishes.
takeaways.zh: 分走部分風頭，不表示原本主角完全消失。

notes: AI-authored provisional draft; independent English, Chinese, media and QA review remain pending. Guide-written source provenance; newly written practice. No human or release approval is implied.

brief.meaningEn: Several parts of a problem or explanation suddenly fit together into a coherent whole.
brief.meaningZh: 問題或解釋的多個部分突然互相吻合，形成清晰的整體。
brief.grammar: A solution or pieces of an explanation click into place; clicked is past. Distinguish this whole-pattern fit from a person simply beginning to understand one point.
brief.register: Everyday learning and problem-solving; a researcher explains how a second look at two records makes a complete sequence coherent.
brief.boundaryZh: 重點是多個線索變得互相吻合；不能只因有人聽懂一個詞便說整個方案已完整。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不是機械零件實際卡進凹槽，也不保證先前每個猜想都正確。
brief.outcomeZh: 能說出哪些線索共同形成解答，以及理解如何轉變。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 190, row 6; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: The solution clicks into place after a second look.

listening.en: The archivist first thought the two dates were unrelated. On a second look, she noticed the same signature and delivery route, and the timeline clicked into place.
listening.zh: 檔案員起初以為兩個日期互不相關。再看一遍時，她注意到相同簽名和運送路線，事件的時間線便突然變得清晰連貫。
listening.promptZh: clicked into place 在這裏表示甚麼？

options.en: The clues formed a coherent sequence.
options.zh: 線索合成了一條清晰連貫的脈絡。

options.en: The dates became unrelated after all.
options.zh: 兩個日期最終變得毫無關聯。

options.en: A file physically snapped into a holder.
options.zh: 檔案實際卡進架子。

options.en: The archivist stopped examining the evidence.
options.zh: 檔案員停止檢視證據。

listening.explanationZh: 相同簽名與路線把兩個日期連成時間線。

reply.promptEn: How did the class finally solve the timetable puzzle? One group matched the room list with the bus arrivals, and then every class had a room and arrival time that fitted.
reply.promptZh: （全班最後怎樣解開時間表難題？一組同學把教室清單與巴士到達時間對照後，每班的教室與到達時間便互相吻合。）

options.en: The two lists now form a consistent schedule.
options.zh: 兩份清單現在合成一致的安排。

options.en: Each class can be placed without a conflict.
options.zh: 每班都可安排而沒有衝突。

options.en: The timetable clicked into place.
options.zh: 時間表突然變得清晰連貫。

options.en: Comparing the lists revealed the overall pattern.
options.zh: 對照清單顯示整體安排。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都描述線索互相吻合形成完整時間表。

scene.promptZh: 技術員再看設備紀錄，發現三次斷電都在同一個測試後發生，故障順序終於清楚。哪句貼切？

options.en: The sequence clicked into place.
options.zh: 整個順序突然變得清晰連貫。

options.en: The records became more contradictory.
options.zh: 紀錄變得更矛盾。

options.en: One cable made a clicking sound.
options.zh: 一條電線發出喀聲。

scene.explanationZh: 三次紀錄顯示一致關係，整體脈絡清楚了。

contrast.promptZh: 哪種情況最不足以說 solution clicked into place？

options.en: A map and delivery logs now explain every stop in order.
options.zh: 地圖與送貨紀錄可按順序解釋每個停站。

options.en: One pupil understands a word, but the rest of the problem remains unresolved.
options.zh: 一名學生聽懂一個詞，但問題其餘部分仍未解決。

options.en: Two experiments and the sensor record fit one explanation.
options.zh: 兩個實驗及感應器紀錄與同一解釋吻合。

contrast.explanationZh: 理解單一詞語不等於多個部分形成完整解答。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「一個學生聽懂一個術語，整個 solution 就 clicked into place。」哪句較準確？

options.en: A solution clicks into place when its parts fit together, not merely when one term is understood.
options.zh: 解答的多個部分互相吻合，才可說突然變得清晰連貫；聽懂一個詞不足夠。

options.en: One term always resolves the whole problem.
options.zh: 聽懂一個詞必定解決整題。

options.en: The phrase requires a real mechanical click.
options.zh: 這片語要求有實際機械卡聲。

dialogue.explanationZh: 此片語聚焦整體線索的配合。

speaking.en: When the rainfall chart matched the reservoir log, the explanation clicked into place: the water level fell after three dry weeks.
speaking.zh: 降雨圖與水庫紀錄吻合後，解釋便突然變得清晰連貫：三週少雨後水位下降。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再指出哪兩份資料互相吻合。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：社區劇團發現後台燈光在三個週末都延遲；場地預約紀錄和電工維修單顯示，每次都在同一個測試時段關電。用英文說明這些線索如何形成完整解釋，但不要聲稱已修好設備。
writing.selfCheckZh: 寫出三個週末的延遲、預約紀錄與維修單、同一測試時段斷電；解釋清楚不等於已修好。

examples.en: The explanation for the theatre’s three weekend lighting delays clicked into place when its booking records and repair slips showed a power shutdown during the same test slot each time; the equipment still needs a fix.
examples.zh: 劇團三個週末燈光延遲的原因，在預約紀錄與維修單都顯示每次同一測試時段斷電後，便有了清晰連貫的解釋；設備仍須維修。

examples.en: After the team compared booking records with the electrician’s slips, the pattern clicked into place: each of the three weekend delays followed a shutdown in the same test slot, though no repair is complete yet.
examples.zh: 團隊對照預約紀錄與電工維修單後，整個規律突然變得清晰連貫：三個週末每次都在同一測試時段斷電後延遲，但設備尚未修妥。

takeaways.en: Click into place means the pieces form a coherent whole.
takeaways.zh: 突然變得清晰連貫，指各部分互相吻合。

takeaways.en: A solution does not click into place merely because one word is understood.
takeaways.zh: 單是聽懂一個詞，不代表整個解答已變得連貫。

notes: AI-authored provisional draft; independent English, Chinese, media and QA review remain pending. Guide-written source provenance; newly written practice. No human or release approval is implied.

brief.meaningEn: Improve mental focus or thinking skill through practice or challenge.
brief.meaningZh: 透過練習或挑戰改善專注力或思考能力。
brief.grammar: An activity can sharpen the mind; the mind is not literally a blade. Avoid promising a guaranteed clinical benefit from a single task.
brief.register: Everyday learning discussion; a teacher explains why comparing multiple possible solutions may train reasoning.
brief.boundaryZh: 着重練習思考能力，不等於證明醫療效果，也不代表每項活動對所有人都相同有效。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不是磨利大腦；一次活動也不能保證永久提升智力。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指出哪項具體思考過程受鍛鍊，並避免無根據的保證。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 190, row 8; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.

listening.en: In the logic club, pupils compare several possible routes and explain why one works. The teacher says that kind of reasoning practice can sharpen the mind.
listening.zh: 在邏輯學會，學生比較幾條可行路線，並解釋為何其中一條可行。老師說，這類推理練習可以鍛鍊思維。
listening.promptZh: sharpen the mind 表示甚麼？

options.en: Practise and improve thinking skills.
options.zh: 練習並改善思考能力。

options.en: Make the brain physically sharp.
options.zh: 令大腦真的變尖。

options.en: Guarantee permanent intelligence after one task.
options.zh: 一次練習就保證智力永久提高。

options.en: Avoid comparing possible routes.
options.zh: 避免比較不同路線。

listening.explanationZh: 比較與解釋路線涉及推理練習。

reply.promptEn: Why does the instructor ask learners to explain two different endings to the story? They must compare evidence and revise their first guess before choosing.
reply.promptZh: （導師為何要求學生解釋故事的兩種結局？他們要比較證據，修正最初猜想，然後作選擇。）

options.en: The task gives them reasoning practice.
options.zh: 任務讓他們練習推理。

options.en: They must test a first idea against evidence.
options.zh: 他們須用證據檢驗最初想法。

options.en: Comparing the endings may sharpen the mind.
options.zh: 比較結局可能鍛鍊思維。

options.en: The activity asks for careful thought rather than a quick guess.
options.zh: 活動要求仔細思考，而非隨便猜測。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都指向有具體比較與修正的思考練習。

scene.promptZh: 學員定期找出數據圖表中的矛盾，並解釋修正方法。哪句貼切？

options.en: The exercise may sharpen the mind.
options.zh: 這種練習可能鍛鍊思維。

options.en: The graph physically cuts the brain.
options.zh: 圖表真的割到大腦。

options.en: One attempt proves a permanent rise in IQ.
options.zh: 一次嘗試證明智商永久提高。

scene.explanationZh: 練習檢查矛盾與解釋方法，涉及思考。

contrast.promptZh: 哪句對 sharpen the mind 最審慎？

options.en: A puzzle is guaranteed to prevent illness.
options.zh: 益智遊戲保證能預防疾病。

options.en: Repeated reasoning practice may help train attention and thinking.
options.zh: 反覆練習推理可能幫助鍛鍊專注與思考。

options.en: Thinking skills improve without any practice.
options.zh: 毋須練習，思考能力也會提升。

contrast.explanationZh: 片語可說思維練習，不構成醫療保證。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「玩一次遊戲就必定永久變聰明。」哪句回應較準確？

options.en: An activity may sharpen the mind through practice, but one game proves no permanent change.
options.zh: 活動可透過練習鍛鍊思維，但玩一次不能證明永久改變。

options.en: The phrase guarantees a permanent effect from one try.
options.zh: 這片語保證一次便有永久效果。

options.en: It means sharpening a real knife.
options.zh: 它表示磨利真正的刀。

dialogue.explanationZh: 不能把練習效果誇大成一次永久提升。

speaking.en: Checking how two maps differ sharpens the mind when it makes students compare details instead of guessing.
speaking.zh: 比較兩張地圖的差異，要求學生細看細節而非猜測，可以鍛鍊思維。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再指出學生練習了哪項思考動作。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：圖書館每週辦一場證據推理小組；參加者比較兩份互有衝突的記錄，找出錯誤日期，並解釋判斷依據。用英文說明這活動如何鍛鍊思維，但不要保證醫療效果。
writing.selfCheckZh: 寫出每週活動、比較兩份矛盾記錄、找出錯誤日期及解釋依據；不作醫療保證。

examples.en: The library’s weekly evidence group may sharpen the mind by having members compare two conflicting records, identify the wrong date and explain their reasoning; that is not a medical guarantee.
examples.zh: 圖書館每週的證據推理小組讓成員比較兩份矛盾紀錄、找出錯誤日期並解釋推理，可能鍛鍊思維；這不是醫療保證。

examples.en: Each week, members compare two inconsistent records and justify which date is wrong. This reasoning practice can sharpen the mind, though the group makes no claim to prevent illness.
examples.zh: 成員每週比較兩份互相矛盾的紀錄，並解釋哪個日期有錯。這種推理練習可以鍛鍊思維，但小組沒有聲稱能預防疾病。

takeaways.en: Sharpen the mind means train thinking through practice.
takeaways.zh: 鍛鍊思維，指透過練習訓練思考能力。

takeaways.en: An activity can sharpen the mind without proving a medical benefit.
takeaways.zh: 活動可以鍛鍊思維，卻不等於已證明醫療效益。

notes: AI-authored provisional draft; independent English, Chinese, media and QA review remain pending. Guide-written source provenance; newly written practice. No human or release approval is implied.

brief.meaningEn: Keep one’s mental alertness or existing skill in good condition through continued use.
brief.meaningZh: 透過持續練習，保持原有的頭腦靈敏或技能水平。
brief.grammar: Stay sharp is intransitive; a person stays sharp, often by doing something. Contrast maintaining a skill with building one from scratch.
brief.register: Informal personal and work discussion; a retired translator explains why she still practises with short passages.
brief.boundaryZh: 強調維持已具備的敏銳度或技能，不是保證完全不退步，也不是新的學習成果。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不是磨利刀具；不能從持續練習直接推斷沒有疾病或衰退。
brief.outcomeZh: 能分辨鍛鍊新能力與維持已有能力，說明持續練習的作用。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 192, row 5; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: My grandfather solves puzzles to stay sharp.

listening.en: After retiring, Nari still translates a short paragraph every morning to stay sharp. She says the daily habit helps her keep using the skills she already has.
listening.zh: 娜莉退休後，每天早上仍翻譯一小段文字，讓自己保持頭腦敏銳。她說，這習慣有助她繼續運用原有技能。
listening.promptZh: stay sharp 在這裏表示甚麼？

options.en: Keep her existing mental skill active.
options.zh: 保持原有的思考技能活躍。

options.en: Start learning translation for the first time.
options.zh: 首次開始學習翻譯。

options.en: Physically sharpen a pencil.
options.zh: 實際削尖鉛筆。

options.en: Prove she can never forget anything.
options.zh: 證明她永遠不會忘事。

listening.explanationZh: 退休後繼續翻譯，是維持已具備的技能。

reply.promptEn: Why does the former radio editor still review a short script each week? She says it keeps her editing judgement active, even though she no longer works full-time.
reply.promptZh: （前電台編輯為何每週仍校閱一篇短稿？她說這能令自己的編輯判斷保持靈敏，雖然已不再全職工作。）

options.en: She wants to keep using a skill she has already developed.
options.zh: 她想繼續運用已培養的技能。

options.en: The weekly review helps maintain her judgement.
options.zh: 每週校閱有助維持她的判斷力。

options.en: She reviews scripts to stay sharp.
options.zh: 她校閱稿件，讓自己保持敏銳。

options.en: The habit gives her regular editing practice.
options.zh: 這習慣讓她定期練習編輯。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都描述持續使用既有編輯能力。

scene.promptZh: 一名資深口譯員每週做模擬口譯，以免反應變慢。哪句貼切？

options.en: She stays sharp by practising each week.
options.zh: 她每週練習，以保持頭腦敏銳。

options.en: She has never interpreted before.
options.zh: 她以前從未做口譯。

options.en: She is sharpening a blade.
options.zh: 她正在磨刀。

scene.explanationZh: 她以練習維持已有的反應與技能。

contrast.promptZh: 哪句對 stay sharp 最審慎？

options.en: Practice guarantees no one will ever become forgetful.
options.zh: 練習保證人永遠不會善忘。

options.en: Continued use may help someone maintain alertness and a practised skill.
options.zh: 持續運用可能有助維持敏銳度和熟練技能。

options.en: It only describes making a knife sharper.
options.zh: 它只描述把刀磨利。

contrast.explanationZh: 片語說維持敏銳，不作絕對健康保證。

dialogue.promptZh: 同學說：「stay sharp 指從零開始學新技能。」哪句回應較準確？

options.en: Stay sharp usually means keep an existing ability active through practice.
options.zh: 保持敏銳通常指透過練習維持已有能力。

options.en: It always means learning something for the first time.
options.zh: 它總指第一次學習。

options.en: It requires a physical sharp object.
options.zh: 它需要真正尖銳的物件。

dialogue.explanationZh: 重點是維持，而不是由零開始。

speaking.en: The former chef tests one recipe a month to stay sharp, keeping her timing and tasting judgement in use.
speaking.zh: 這名前廚師每月測試一道食譜，以保持敏銳，繼續運用對時間和味道的判斷。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說出她想維持哪兩項判斷。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：已退休的舞台燈光師每週分析一份舊演出燈光圖，並練習解釋快速換場；她已具備這些技能，只想保持判斷敏銳。用英文說明她的習慣，不要說她由零開始學。
writing.selfCheckZh: 寫出退休、每週分析舊燈光圖、練習解釋快速換場、維持已有技能。

examples.en: The retired lighting designer studies an old show plan each week and explains rapid scene changes to stay sharp; she is maintaining skills she already has.
examples.zh: 這名退休燈光師每週分析一份舊演出燈光圖，並解釋快速換場，以保持敏銳；她是在維持已有技能。

examples.en: To stay sharp, the former stage lighting designer reviews a past lighting plan weekly and practises explaining quick scene transitions rather than learning the job from scratch.
examples.zh: 這名前舞台燈光師每週檢視一份舊燈光圖，並練習解釋快速換場，以保持頭腦敏銳，而非由零開始學習這份工作。

takeaways.en: Stay sharp means keep existing alertness or skill active.
takeaways.zh: 保持頭腦敏銳，指維持已有的靈敏度或技能。

takeaways.en: Practising to stay sharp does not guarantee a person will never decline.
takeaways.zh: 練習以保持敏銳，不保證一個人永不退步。

brief.meaningEn: Get up and walk or move briefly after sitting for a while.
brief.meaningZh: 坐了一段時間後起身短暫走動、伸展雙腿。
brief.grammar: Stretch one’s legs; the possessive agrees with the person walking. Often used for a short break on a trip or during work.
brief.register: Everyday travel and work talk; a driver suggests a short stop so seated passengers can move before continuing.
brief.boundaryZh: 重點是短暫活動身體，不等於正式健身，也不表示旅程已結束。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不必真的做拉筋動作；也不能從一次短暫走動推斷已完成長時間運動。
brief.outcomeZh: 能區分中途起身走走與終點到達或正式運動。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 193, row 3; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: The passengers stopped by the river to stretch their legs.

listening.en: After two hours on the coach, the passengers stopped at a rest area to stretch their legs. They walked for ten minutes before boarding again.
listening.zh: 乘客坐了兩小時旅遊巴後，在休息站停車起身走走。他們步行十分鐘後又上車。
listening.promptZh: stretch their legs 在這裏表示甚麼？

options.en: Take a short walking break after sitting.
options.zh: 坐了一段時間後短暫走動。

options.en: Finish the journey at the rest area.
options.zh: 在休息站完成旅程。

options.en: Join a formal training session.
options.zh: 參加正式訓練課。

options.en: Remain seated for another two hours.
options.zh: 再坐兩小時不動。

listening.explanationZh: 十分鐘後再上車，屬中途短暫走動。

reply.promptEn: Why did the editor pause the four-hour screening? Everyone had been sitting without a break, so she gave them ten minutes to walk around the foyer before the film resumed.
reply.promptZh: （編輯為何暫停四小時的放映？大家一直坐着，沒有休息；她給眾人十分鐘在大堂走走，然後繼續放映。）

options.en: She wanted viewers to move briefly after sitting.
options.zh: 她想觀眾久坐後短暫活動。

options.en: The film was only paused, not cancelled.
options.zh: 電影只是暫停，並非取消。

options.en: She let them stretch their legs.
options.zh: 她讓觀眾起身走走。

options.en: The break ended before the screening resumed.
options.zh: 放映恢復前，休息已結束。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都與久坐後短暫走動、再繼續放映相符。

scene.promptZh: 長途火車中途停十分鐘，旅客下車在月台走動後回到座位。哪句貼切？

options.en: They stopped to stretch their legs.
options.zh: 他們停下來起身走走。

options.en: They arrived at their final destination.
options.zh: 他們已到達終點。

options.en: They began an hour-long workout.
options.zh: 他們開始一小時健身。

scene.explanationZh: 只是中途短暫活動，仍會繼續旅程。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個情境最不符合 stretch their legs？

options.en: Workers walk around the corridor during a short break.
options.zh: 員工短暫休息時在走廊走動。

options.en: A passenger stays in the same seat throughout the stop.
options.zh: 乘客整個停站期間都坐在原位。

options.en: Drivers leave the vehicle for a brief walk before continuing.
options.zh: 司機繼續行程前下車短暫走走。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「stretch their legs 一定要做專業拉筋。」哪句較準確？

options.en: Stretch their legs can simply mean get up and walk briefly after sitting.
options.zh: 起身走走可以只是久坐後短暫步行。

options.en: It always means a formal exercise class.
options.zh: 它一定指正式運動課。

options.en: It means the trip is over.
options.zh: 它表示旅程已結束。

dialogue.explanationZh: 片語常指短暫走動，不要求正式伸展訓練。

speaking.en: After the long workshop, the trainees stretched their legs in the courtyard for five minutes, then returned for the final session.
speaking.zh: 長時間工作坊後，學員到庭院起身走走五分鐘，再回來上最後一節。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再指出走動持續多久以及之後做甚麼。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：審稿團隊連續坐了三小時，主持人安排八分鐘走廊休息，大家起身走動後回來繼續討論最後兩篇文章。用英文描述短暫休息，勿說工作已結束或已完成健身。
writing.selfCheckZh: 寫出連坐三小時、八分鐘走廊走動、回來討論最後兩篇文章；勿說活動已完。

examples.en: After three hours seated, the reviewers used an eight-minute corridor break to stretch their legs, then returned to discuss the final two articles.
examples.zh: 審稿團隊連續坐了三小時後，利用八分鐘走廊休息起身走走，然後回來討論最後兩篇文章。

examples.en: The chair paused the review after three hours so the team could stretch their legs in the corridor for eight minutes; they then resumed work on the last two articles.
examples.zh: 主持人於連續三小時審稿後暫停會議，讓團隊在走廊起身走走八分鐘；之後他們恢復討論最後兩篇文章。

takeaways.en: Stretch one’s legs means take a short walking break after sitting.
takeaways.zh: 起身走走，指久坐後短暫步行活動。

takeaways.en: To stretch their legs, passengers need not finish the journey or join a workout.
takeaways.zh: 乘客起身走走，不代表旅程結束或參加正式健身。
